description: The Valkyries, in just their second season, swept the reigning champion Aces in the semifinals

The Valkyries, in just their second season, swept the reigning champion Aces in the semifinals

        Just over three years ago, on Oct. 5, 2023, the Golden State Valkyries were officially introduced as the WNBA's first expansion team in over a decade. At the introductory press conference, more than a year before the team even had any players, let alone took the court for the first time, team owner Joe Lacob made a bold proclamation. "First press conference with the Warriors, I said we will win a championship in the first five years," Lacob said. "I'm telling you right now, we will win a WNBA championship in the first five years of this franchise."After completing a sweep of the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces on Friday with a thrilling 87-77 overtime victory in Game 3 of the semifinals, the Valkyries have advanced to the WNBA Finals for the first time in franchise history and are four wins away from making Lacob look like a genius. They'll face the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals, beginning on Oct. 17.
The Valkyries made history in their inaugural season in 2025 when they set a record for wins by an expansion team (23) and became the first expansion franchise to make the playoffs in their inaugural season. Despite the initial success, expectations weren't high entering 2026, especially after a somewhat confusing offseason highlighted by trading their first-round pick (Flau'jae Johnson) for two second-round picks. 
But the Valkyries' strong belief in their internal development proved well-founded, and they were bolstered by the arrival of free-agent signings Gabby Williams and Kiah Stokes, who helped make their defense so overwhelming that it made up for their continued issues on the offensive end. The Valkyries didn't have a single player average more than 15 points per game, finished seventh in offensive rating (108.2), which was the second-worst mark of any playoff team, and were 13th in true shooting (54%), above only the Seattle Storm and Connecticut Sun, the two worst teams in the league. But on the other end, the Valkyries had one of the best defenses in WNBA history. Their 99.1 defensive rating was more than four points per 100 possessions better than any other team, and they finished second in both opponent true shooting (53.5%) and opponent turnover rate (19.2%). 
Their defensive-minded approach carried them to a 32-10 record -- a nine-win improvement on last season -- and the No. 2 seed in the playoffs. It almost cost them in the first round, however, when they shot 35.1% in a winner-take-all Game 3 against the Dallas Wings, and had to pull off a stunning 16-point comeback to keep their season alive. Their offense was a bit better against the Aces, but once again, their defense stepped up to save the day. The Aces were 3-0 against the Valkyries in the regular season, in large part because A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young did whatever they wanted in those contests. Those two were held in check in the semis. Wilson had 23 points per game on 41.1% shooting, while Young put up just 14.3 points on 31.6% from the field. As a team, the Aces' true shooting was 50.8% -- nearly 10 percent worse than their 59.3% mark in the regular season. During the series-clinching victory on Friday, the Valkyries completed an 11-point comeback in the second half in large part because they held the Aces to just two points over the first eight minutes and 25 seconds of the third quarter. Las Vegas went just 2 of 16 from the field in that frame. 
Williams, who made her second All-Star appearance this season and finished as the runner-up to Angel Reese for Defensive Player of the Year, averaged 20.3 points to lead the way in the series, while Kayla Thornton put up 14 points and Tiffany Hayes chipped in 11.7. As a team, the Valkyries shot 39.8% from the field, had a true shooting mark of 54% and barely had more assists (41) than turnovers (40). And yet, they're going to the Finals. We've simply never seen an organization or a team like the Valkyries.

description: Atlanta, powered by Reese and Jordin Canada, pulled off the sweep with a two-point win on the road

Atlanta, powered by Reese and Jordin Canada, pulled off the sweep with a two-point win on the road

        The Atlanta Dream advanced to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013 in thrilling fashion with an 85-83 victory over the New York Liberty in Game 3 of their semifinal series. After a three-game sweep of the Liberty, the Dream will face the Golden State Valkyries in the Finals, which will begin on Oct. 17. The Dream jumped in front early in an extremely physical contest that nearly got out of hand on multiple occasions as the officials let just about everything go. Notably, Angel Reese got in Sabrina Ionescu's face after the Liberty guard delivered a hard foul to Isobel Borlase as payback for what she thought should have been a foul on Borlase. And later, both Reese and Jonquel Jones were hit with technicals after a dust-up under the basket. Early in the second half, the Dream pushed their lead up to 12, but the Liberty immediately responded and took a lead of their own into the fourth. When Ionescu hit a 3-pointer 30 seconds into the final frame to push the Liberty's lead to five, it seemed they might pull away. Instead, it became a back-and-forth affair down the stretch. After Jordin Canada hit a circus shot to give the Dream a four-point advantage with just over a minute to play, Jones responded to cut the deficit to two. The Liberty then got a few stops and had multiple chances to tie the game. One ended with a Ionescu turnover -- she had a crucial turnover at the end of Game 2 as well -- and the other ended with a miss by Breanna Stewart. 
DeWanna Bonner, who stepped up yet again in this postseason with 13 points and 13 rebounds, then iced the game at the free throw line. Canada, who was tremendous all series, finished with 19 points, 11 assists and no turnovers, while Reese had 22 points and nine rebounds. Jones was excellent for the Liberty in defeat with 26 points, 14 rebounds and three blocks, while Stewart, who was swept for the first time in her illustrious career, added 26 points of her own. The Dream have been to the Finals three times, but have been swept on every occasion. They'll look to change that trend this time, and potentially win the first title in franchise history. As the Dream await the 2026 Finals, here's a look at how they swept the Liberty. 
Dominating on the marginsAllisha Gray played 11 minutes in this series due to a hand injury, Rhyne Howard shot 19 of 61 (31.1%) from the field. the Liberty won or tied 8/13 periods (including the overtime) and shot 47.1% compared to the Dream's 41.9%. And yet, the Dream pulled off a sweep. How? In large part by dominating on the margins. Just look at the difference in some of these key categories:TeamTov. ForcedPts. Off Tov.Off. Reb.Second Chance Pts.Fastbreak Pts.Dream4972293436Liberty3031204010The Dream forced 19 more turnovers, scored a staggering 41 more points off turnovers, grabbed nine more offensive rebounds and scored 26 more fastbreak points. The Liberty's only victory in the margins was a narrow one in second-chance points. Thanks to their ability to force turnovers and control the offensive glass, the Dream took 33 more field goal attempts and 11 more free throw attempts, which made up for the fact that they were far less efficient from the floor. TeamFGAFG%FTAFT%Dream22441.9%7087.1%Liberty19147.1%5986.4%Reese deliversAs well as Angel Reese played down the stretch this season, there were still some questions about how she would fare in her first postseason. And they didn't go away when she went 4 of 15 from the field in Game 1 of the Dream's first-round series with the Mystics. But since then, she's been awesome on both ends of the floor. In three games against the Liberty, she averaged 20.7 points, 7.7 rebounds, two steals and 2.3 blocks on 47.7% shooting. For the series, she was second on the team in scoring, second in rebounding, first in steals and first in blocks. The Dream were also plus-21 in Reese's 110 minutes, the second-best plus-minus on the team. Reese's work on the offensive glass -- she grabbed 14 of the team's 29 offensive rebounds in the series -- was crucial to their ability to dominate on the margins, and she was completely disruptive on the defensive end, both on and off the ball. In addition, she brought an edge that the Liberty too often failed to match. 
Canada leads role player renaissanceAgain, Gray, who led the team in scoring in the regular season at 19 points per game, played 11 minutes and Howard scored 55 points on 61 shots. If you knew that going into the series, you would have assumed the Liberty swept the Dream, not the other way around. In addition to dominating on the margins, the Dream got huge performances from a number of role players throughout the series. No one was more impressive than Jordin Canada, who played the best basketball of her career at the perfect time. Canada, who won titles with the Seattle Storm as the back-up to Sue Bird in 2018 and 2020, had played 22 playoff games in her first eight seasons. She had scored 19 or more points just once, back in 2019; she did so in all three games against the Liberty, while also playing stellar defense and taking nearly perfect care of the ball. For the series, Canada averaged 22.3 points on 62.2/61.5/100 shooting splits, along with 7.7 assists and two steals. She led the team in scoring, assists, steals and field goal percentage, and had just six total turnovers in 110 minutes. Just look at the difference between her numbers in the regular season and this series. 
Canada's finishing at the rim stood out as almost unbelievable, especially against the Liberty's size, which MVP runner-up Olivia Miles look completely out of depth. Canada was 13 of 17 (76.5%) at the rim in the series, and for the entire playoffs is now 16 of 24 (66.7%). Among the 11 playes with at least 20 rim attempts in the postseason, the only ones who have been more efficient than Canada are all elite bigs. PlayerRim FGRim FGARim FG%Jonquel Jones232882.1%Breanna Stewart202580%Aliyah Boston162272.7%A'ja Wilson172568%Jordin Canada162466.7%In addition to Canada, the Dream got 15.3 points and a team-leading 8.3 rebounds from DeWanna Bonner, who didn't join the team until late August after she was waived by the Phoenix Mercury. Rookie guard Isobel Borlase, who barely played in Game 1, took on a bigger role in Gray's absence and chipped in 21 points on 9 of 15 in Games 2 and 3. As a group, Canada, Bonner and Borlase shot 15 of 31 (48.4%) from 3-point range. During the regular season, Canada shot 29.2%, Bonner shot 27.9% and Borlase shot 32.4% from behind the arc.

        USC wide receiver Terrell Anderson will undergo season-ending surgery, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Anderson was a huge pick-up for the Trojans in the transfer portal, but his season is over after just three games and two receptions for 50 yards.A four-star recruit coming out of high school, Anderson spent the first two seasons of his college career at NC State, where he broke out as a sophomore in 2025. Last fall, Anderson totaled 39 receptions for 629 yards and five touchdowns.When Anderson entered the portal, there was plenty of interest in him, given his unique combination of size and skill. He was ranked as the No. 10 overall transfer, according to 247Sports. When the Trojans signed Anderson, he was viewed as a potential superstar with Jayden Maiava throwing him the football.
Unfortunately for Maiava and the Trojans, the injury has impacted Anderson throughout the season. He missed the season-opener against Fresno State, and he played only sparingly in the last three games. Anderson recorded two receptions for 50 yards in a loss to Oregon, but that's the only time he appeared on the stat sheet outside of punt returns.
With Anderson on the shelf for the remainder of the season, USC will need production from other players in the passing game, but the receiver room has been banged up in the early going.Injury bug biting USC pass-catchersAnderson isn't the only key receiver who has dealt with injuries in Los Angeles. Freshman wideout Trent Mosley got off to a terrific start with 255 yards and four touchdowns in three games. However, he's been sidelined for the last two games after suffering a knee injury.Freshman tight end Mark Bowman, the No. 42 overall player in the 2026 signing class, is also dealing with an injury after missing the Washington game last week. How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers     There are a number of different wagering options available on each race, and here we will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that define bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.           Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds           Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.             What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.            The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                     Win           The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                      Place           The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.            Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                       Show           A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                       Win/Place           Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                       Place/Show           The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                       Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)            Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.            It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                       The most popular horse racing bet types           Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).            It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.           Exactas           An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                       Trifectas           This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.            The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                       Superfectas           Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                      Super High 5           Some books will even allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                      Box           A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.            For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:           $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:           $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.            A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                       How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers           While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                       Daily Double           The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.            Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                       Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6           Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.           Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.            The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                       Understanding horse racing payouts           After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.            The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:           2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           				           $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				           If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.            For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:            2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				          Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting          The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.           October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes           Triple Crown of horse racing           The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.            Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.            The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                       Tips and advice for betting on horse racing           There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                       Racing forms and past performances           These are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                       Track conditions           Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                       Horse tendencies            From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.            The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                       Post position           Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                      Trainer and jockey information           A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                       Workout times           There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                       Speed figures           Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.            Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                      Manage your horse racing betting bankroll           Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                       Rules and responsible gaming           Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.           Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.           FAQHow to bet on horse racing?There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.How to bet on horse racing online?Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.What is a box bet in horse racing?A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.What is a show bet in horse racing?A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.What is a key box bet in horse racing?A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

body:
Philadelphia's offense could be stuck in the mud once again on Sunday

        The Philadelphia Eagles' (2-2) offense is officially in free fall. Philadelphia is coming off an epic meltdown home defeat against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 in which they blew a double-digit lead and went 0-12 in third-down conversion attempts. In the wake of that loss, Eagles six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday, and the team then traded two-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens. That's on top of their CVS receipt-length injury list, which includes 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), both being ruled out ahead of Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) in London.
That means Week 5 could look a lot like Week 4. Quarterback Jalen Hurts completed just 12 of his 27 throws for 93 yards while taking four sacks. That all added up to a career-low 3.0 yards per dropback. Since Week 3, Hurts is averaging an NFL-worst 4.7 yards per pass attempt after ranking 11th best in the league in that same metric with a 7.5 yards per pass average through the first two weeks of the season. The good news for the Eagles is that even with a loss in Week 5, the NFC East will likely remain up for grabs. The New York Giants are 3-1, but their ceiling is capped by the season-ending knee injury to quarterback Jaxson Dart. Fill-in Jameis Winston ranks dead last in the NFL in completion percentage at 55.1% this season. The Giants are also without three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Brian Burns, their best pass rusher, whose 16.5 sacks ranked second in the league in 2025, for the rest of the year after he tore his ACL and meniscus. The Washington Commanders are 1-3, and quarterback Jayden Daniels is once again dealing with an elbow injury. 
It will be interesting to see how head coach Nick Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion adjust to the absences of both their star playmakers, with the team facing a schematic clash early in the season.

title: How Bob Chesney made Curt Cignetti's blueprint his own to rebuild UCLA - CBS Sports
description: The former James Madison coach brought in a gaggle of transfers to quickly turn around what had been a dysfunctio
body:
The former James Madison coach brought in a gaggle of transfers to quickly turn around what had been a dysfunctional UCLA program
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The comparisons between Bob Chesney and Curt Cignetti are numerous. Both worked their way up as journeymen from the lower levels of the sport, stacking double-digit-win teams and even placing players in the NFL. For Chesney, his path took him from Division III Salve Regina to Division II Assumption to FCS Holy Cross. Conference championships followed at each stop.Both coached at James Madison, where they led the Dukes to conference championships and, for Chesney, a spot in the 12-team playoff. Both moved to down-on-their-luck Big Ten basketball schools and brought in players they were familiar with to help revamp their rosters. Thirteen JMU players followed Cignetti to Bloomington, and seven remained on the national title roster. UCLA has a dozen former Dukes on its roster, and roughly half are significant contributors.A key difference in roster build is the perceived level of talent. Whereas Indiana ranked 72nd in the 247Sports Talent Composite coming into last season, UCLA is 24th in 2026, largely due to the retention of key players, notably five-star Nico Iamaleava.At Indiana, Cignetti has capped one of the great turnaround stories in the sport's history with a national title. In Chesney's case, he hopes his import will also produce program-changing results. It's certainly too early to tell, but how are these Bruins built? CBS Sports goes inside the roster to break it down.
Note: If the player is a transfer, the star rating is his 247Sports transfer rating, not his high school rating. "(2025)" denotes a player in UCLA's 2025 transfer class, and therefore inherited by Chesney.QuarterbackNico Iamaleava — Sr. | Transfer from Tennessee | ★★★★★ (2025)According to Iamaleava, it only took one meeting to convince him that staying at UCLA and close to home was the right decision. Chesney has been clear that retaining him was key in bridging the culture past the dysfunction of the 2025 season. So far, his legs have been the bigger asset than his arm, but his leadership has been key.Running BackWayne Knight — 5th Yr. | Transfer from James Madison | ★★★Anthony Woods — 5th Yr. | Transfer from Utah | ★★★ (2025)
The team's current star and most productive offensive player had to be talked into coming back to a James Madison team he'd been estranged from when Chesney arrived in Harrisonburg. He fielded offers from other schools last offseason but decided to follow Chesney to LA in the portal.Four games into the season, he paces one of the country's best rushing attacks with a stunning 9.08 yards per carry. He is simply on a tear and currently has more rushing touchdowns than 30 Power Four teams."I know this guy wins," Knight said about Chesney to the school's website. "He wants to talk to his players. He wants to get to know you and know your journey and just know what kind of person you are. So, you can not only be a better player for him, but a better man after it's all said and done."
Wide ReceiverPlayerClassTransfer FromRatingBrian Rowe Jr.So.South Carolina★★★Landon EllisSr.James Madison★★★Semaj MorganSr.Michigan★★★UCLA's passing game has yet to truly get going (Morgan leads in receptions with 14 so far this season), but it hasn't had to, considering how well the Bruins have controlled games on the ground.Tight EndPlayerClassTransfer FromRatingBrayden Loftin5th Yr.Kansas State★★★Harry Lodge5th Yr.Wake Forest★★★In a passing game that isn't prolific, UCLA's tight ends are most often used as extra run blockers.Offensive LinePlayerClassTransfer FromRatingJordan Davis5th Yr.South Alabama★★★Eugene BrooksJr.Oklahoma★★★ (2025)Riley RobellSr.James Madison★★★Carter Sweazie5th Yr.James Madison★★★Hall Schmidt5th Yr.Boise State★★★Jensen SomervilleJr.—★★★The most intriguing part of Chesney's James Madison import is that it includes two interior offensive linemen in Sweazie and Robell. The interior is where height and length are a bit less of a concern than at tackle, especially regarding Sweazie, who is a 6-foot-1 guard. But they plow the road for one of the nation's most efficient run games, and they're part of a unit that includes other Group of Six players identified by UCLA's personnel staff as contributors.
Defensive LinePlayerClassTransfer FromRatingAshton SandersSr.Oklahoma★★★ (2025)Tyson Ford5th Yr.California★★★Sahir WestJr.James Madison★★★★Aiden Gobaira5th Yr.James Madison★★★A.J. FuimaonoSr.—★★★Darold DeNgoheSr.Rutgers★★★Amier WashingtonSr.Texas Tech★★★West and Gobaira anchor a defensive line on the edges that rotates heavily at most spots. Rotation can keep a unit fresh, as it does for the Bruins, as does having huge leads in most of the games they've played so far this season. Against Oregon, the task will be sizable against a sixable offensive line out to prove its early-season struggles were an aberration.LinebackerPlayerClassTransfer FromRatingJalen Woods5th Yr.—★★★Sammy OmosighoSr.Oklahoma★★★★Scott TaylorSo.—★★★The gem here is Omosigho, who is emerging as one of the nation's best linebackers with 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks already this year. He was lost in the shuffle at OU but has found a place with, as he said this spring, "an opportunity." It's a group Pleasant at least is familiar with due to his time in Eugene, and Barksdale, like the rest of the Dukes who came over last season, got familiar with in the Playoff last season.
SafetyPlayerClassTransfer FromRatingMalik HartfordSr.Ohio State★★★Ta'Shawn JamesSr.Iowa State★★★James has been a magnet for the ball so far this year on the back end with three interceptions. Only one player in the country has more. He pairs nicely with Malik Hartford, who recovered from shoulder surgery in 2025 to contribute in LA this season.

title: Arteta says conscious clear over time at Manchester City - CBS Sports
description: Newly committed to north London through 2030, the reigning champion brushed off questions regarding City's allege
body:
Newly committed to north London through 2030, the reigning champion brushed off questions regarding City's alleged rule breaches to focus on turning his side into the best in the world
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Arsenal have spent the last week talking themselves up as the coming force in world football, a club who believe they can be the best in the game for years to come and are prepared to say so repeatedly. Their manager, the only man in the Premier League with a winners' medal in his back pocket, has just put pen to paper on a contract that will extend his spell for a decade.And that was at best this week's B plot. Such is the gravitational pull of the Manchester City story. It is one that Mikel Arteta was always going to find himself drawn into. No manager can say they have experienced a Premier League warped by City quite like Arteta. As a player, he arrived at the Emirates Stadium a week after Samir Nasri had upped sticks for the Etihad. His coaching career began under Pep Guardiola, two of his three and a half years as an assistant falling within the period of the 114 breaches of Premier League rules. Then, of course, came the defining period of his career so far, the long and ultimately glorious battle against City for Premier League supremacy.There was plenty Arteta might have shared. Little he chose to. Ultimately, the nearest he got to a definitive statement on City was when asked, given his time at the club, whether his conscience was clear. "Yes," he said emphatically. That aside, the Spaniard was even more cagey on his former employers than he would be when asked about a high-profile injury. It was easy to see why Arteta might be reticent to speak for a club that has reserved the right to explore legal avenues against City once the Premier League's case has been concluded. He was no more candid, however, when it came to reflecting his own personal experience of that momentous day in Premier League history when the charges dropped."This has been going for various years," he said. "That process is still not finished. So it is very difficult to express how I feel, because it is not resolved. When it is resolved, I can talk with clarity and tell you exactly how I feel."
He will be held to that. Few came to London Colney expecting Arteta to expound on the City situation. Even if it weren't for his ties to the Etihad, it is just not his style to concern himself with many matters beyond his team, the crusade for more substitutes on the bench notwithstanding. The media room gravitas of reigning Premier League champion does not sit as easily on Arteta as it did, for instance, on Jurgen Klopp, let alone Arsene Wenger.Arteta was not the only one to play the many questions over City with a dead bat (this is a cricket reference for all you Americans out there). Andoni Iraola was similarly circumspect, ahead of his side's confrontation with City this weekend, though it was notable that Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, who might have had more Premier League winners' medals had it not been for City's rule-breaking, called for speed in concluding this process. That is a view shared by many other clubs in the Premier League, though on Friday's evidence Arteta was in no rush to resume questions over his past.His future seemed far more invigorating now that he is signed up to 2030. An extension to terms due to expire at the end of this season had long been expected; what was more notable was the way in which club and manager reached an agreement to prolong their partnership beyond the decade mark. Even when they end with one being the best-paid manager in the Premier League, few managers find themselves saying that they "loved" the negotiations after fresh terms have been agreed. Arteta is different.
He loved "the way we have analysed what we've done together and especially how we're going to take this club to be the best in the world for many years... You just have a sense how you feel about each other, how we do things, and I feel really lucky and having [co-chairs] Stan and Josh [Kroenke] in front of you and talking to them and expressing still what they want to do, how they want to do it, especially is just inspiring."That is not the first time since signing his new deal that Arteta has set expectations at a stratospheric level. Last season's Premier League title was, he said, just the beginning. Meanwhile, club chief executive Richard Garlick spoke about Arsenal "[dominating] football for the next number of years". That is a big ask for a team with one top-flight title to their name in 22 years, one that is still without that Champions League win that is a prerequisite of elite status. These are also the sort of lines that can come back to haunt a team, and yet Arteta is not afraid of setting the bar at the highest level."I don't think you have to hide it; the thing is that you have to earn it every single day. Your aspirations and your dreams are where they are. I think it's easier to get them [now]. If I said to you the one that I had when I arrived [as manager in 2019], probably you would say what are you talking about? 
"That was the ambition, that's the drive, and it's because we believe that we can do it, and then there will be many factors that would allow us or not to achieve it. Time will tell, but certainly that drive is there."And of course that opportunity to establish Arsenal as the leading lights in England and Europe is all the greater with their rivals facing what seems likely to be a cataclysmic set of sanctions. Not, of course, that Arteta would want to discuss it in those terms.

title: Eagles releasing veteran QB Andy Dalton, still unsettled at QB2 behind Jalen Hurts - CBS Sports
description: Dalton will begin the process of finding a new team

Dalton will begin the process of finding a new team

        The Philadelphia Eagles have made a surprise personnel move as they prepare for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. The team has released veteran quarterback Andy Dalton, according to multiple reports. Dalton, who will turn 39 later this month, was intercepted in his only pass attempt this season. It occurred in the end zone during the first half of Philadelphia's eventual Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears when Jalen Hurts temporarily left the game after getting hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson. 
Dalton's spot on the Eagles' depth chart will be replaced by Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton. McKee, a 2023 sixth-round pick, has made one start in the last two years. He has five career touchdown passes and one interception and has completed 61.4% of his passes. Payton, a fifth-round pick in this year's draft, has yet to play in a regular-season game.While the Eagles adjust their quarterback room, Dalton will begin his search for a new team. A three-time Pro Bowler, Dalton spent his first nine NFL seasons with the Bengals, with whom he helped lead to the playoffs five straight seasons from 2011-16. He has also spent time with the Saints, Bears and Panthers. 
In his career, Dalton has thrown for 39,793 yards, 254 touchdowns, and 152 interceptions. He has completed 62.6% of his passes. Where will Dalton end up next? Here are a few possible landing spots. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    VikingsMinnesota could use another backup quarterback after it traded JJ McCarthy to the Giants. In Dalton, the Vikings would have two veteran quarterbacks behind Kyler Murray, alongside Carson Wentz. Wentz played well earlier this season after Murray sustained an injury. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Giants Speaking of the Giants, they could also use a veteran quarterback after losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury. Jameis Winston is coming off his best game as a Giant, but it's safe to say that the Giants would still benefit from having another quarterback in the room. However, after acquiring JJ McCarthy, it's unlikely they're willing to make another move.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Saints This is a situation where Dalton could serve as a mentor for Tyler Shough, whose season so far has had its share of ups and downs. At this point, Shough does not have a mentor in the quarterback room. His current backup is Spencer Rattler, who is a year younger than he is. Dalton could be a valuable sounding board for a young room looking for some guidance.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dolphins Like New Orleans, Dalton could serve as a mentor in Miami for Malik Willis, who is currently entrenched in his first season as a full-time starter. Willis' current backup, Kyle McCord, is also in his first year with the Dolphins and has yet to play in an NFL regular-season game. But the question remains whether the tanking Dolphins would go after a quarterback now or get their pick during the 2027 NFL Draft. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TitansAnother team where Dalton could help a young quarterback find his footing. Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, is still growing as a starting quarterback. It's safe to assume that a player with Dalton's experience would help him with his continued development.

title: Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles to meet in Week 5: Did Giants make right choice between first-round linebackers? - CBS Sports
description: There might not have been a wrong answer for the Giants at pick No. 5 in the 2026 NFL Draft
body:
There might not have been a wrong answer for the Giants at pick No. 5 in the 2026 NFL Draft
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When the Washington Commanders host the New York Giants on Sunday, keep an eye on No. 52. Both of them.There is a striking parallel between the two teams: Both have a first-round rookie linebacker from Ohio State who wears the same number as the other. Giants standout Arvell Reese and burgeoning Commanders star Sonny Styles became the first college linebacker teammates to be selected in the top 10 of the same NFL Draft when they flew off the board in April. In Week 5, they go head-to-head.At the draft, the Giants were in the enviable position of having both Reese and Styles available to them at pick No. 5. There was immense debate prior to draft night about which player New York should select if both were up for grabs. After the event, a major question was whether they took the right one.In the end, there might not have been a wrong answer. The case for Arvell ReeseThat the Giants are off to a 3-1 start despite being without quarterback Jaxson Dart for nearly three full games is largely a credit to Reese and the defense. New York is a top-10 team in yards and points allowed through Week 4, and Reese is the engine that powers the unit. Not only does he pace the team with 33 tackles, but he also leads the entire league in solo stops with 26.
Reese is also fresh off the best game of his young career: a nine-tackle effort with one tackle for loss in a 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The NFL recognized him as the Week 4 Rookie of the Week after he became the fifth Giants rookie with three passes defended and an interception in one game.
The production is already game-changing. It is everything the Giants could have asked for when they used their first of two first-round picks on a linebacker. Reese's utility goes well beyond the numbers, though. His versatility proved to be a major asset across four games for a Giants defense that lost its top edge rusher, Brian Burns, for the season with a torn ACL. Reese's pass-rushing ability from the off-ball linebacker spot will be crucial the rest of the year as the Giants work to overcome the absence of Burns, who last year amassed 16.5 sacks in an All-Pro campaign.Reese is a more natural pass-rusher than Styles, which is an obvious asset, but at the draft, there was hesitation over whether he was the better pick. The Giants were already stocked at the edge rusher position with Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux providing both top-flight play in the starting lineup and enviable depth. With one of them out for the year, though, Reese is even more important to the unit than he already was. He is a linebacker first and likely always will be, but Reese can also play in the trenches. In his debut, even with Burns healthy, he aligned on the line of scrimmage on 11 of 52 snaps.
The case for Sonny StylesReese is exactly what the Giants hoped they were getting when they picked him. But who's to say Sonny Styles would not have been the same? He could have been just as impactful, had he been the No. 5 pick instead.When the Commanders upset the Seahawks in Week 3, Styles looked the part of a star in the making. He earned the NFC Defensive Player of the Week award for his efforts, which also made him the first rookie linebacker in franchise history with an interception, a forced fumble and multiple passes defended in one game.Styles' ability to wreak havoc in the backfield with inside pressure is also tremendous. He boasts the highest pressure rate among rookie defenders with at least 25 pass-rush snaps at 17.9%. The Commanders are about as aggressive as they come in pass defense with the second-highest blitz rate in the league, per Next Gen Stats, and Styles is a key figure in that scheme as they regularly rush him toward the quarterback.
And then there was this play, where Styles demolished Saquon Barkley en route to a sack.
While they attack the pocket from different angles, Styles and Reese are both impact pass-rushers. Perhaps the Giants would have been better off with Styles, given their depth on the edge.Styles has stepped up in the face of injuries just like Reese. Leo Chenal and Jordan Magee are both on injured reserve, leaving Styles, Frankie Luvu and Kain Medrano as the only three available inside linebackers. Not only that, but Styles routinely handles the defense's green-dot duties, relaying play calls to the rest of the unit as just a rookie. There is a chance he could have secured that job with the Giants, too, considering New York relies on 2026 newcomer Tremaine Edmunds to orchestrate the defense. Styles has a whole lot on his plate for someone with only four games of experience, and is not just getting by. He is thriving.
Verdict: It's a washIn hindsight, the Giants found themselves in a win-win position at the draft. With Reese and Styles as their targets, they could not have gone wrong. What both players displayed over the first four games of their professional careers proved that New York could have gone in either direction and come away with the same result, at least for the first month of the year. The final analysis will not be complete for years, when their career arcs take full shape, but as of now, the Ohio State products are on level footing.If the argument for Reese was that he is the better pass rusher, then Styles bridged the gap with his effective blitzes. If the argument for Styles was that he is the better defender in coverage, then Reese closed that discrepancy. According to Pro Football Focus, Reese graded out over four games as the ninth-best linebacker in coverage, while Styles is a mere six spots ahead of him at No. 3. In a sample size of 74 qualified linebackers, both are excellent.Both are top-five rookie linebackers in overall PFF defensive grade.Rookie LBPFF Defensive GradeHarold Perkins Jr., Falcons82.6Josiah Trotter, Buccaneers79.2Arvell Reese, Giants77.1Sonny Styles, Commanders76.9Jaishawn Barham, Cowboys69.1Reese has the second-best odds to win Defensive Rookie of the Year at +275, and Styles is directly behind him with the third-shortest odds at +750, per DraftKings. The margin between their first-year production is extremely thin, and both carry long-term stardom potential. The Giants ought to feel elated about their choice in the draft, and the Commanders should, too.

body:
Emma Hayes gets two cracks at the world's best as Ashley Sanchez returns in elite form and Trinity Rodman leads a dynamic attack
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This international break, soccer fans will be in for a treat as the number one and number two women's national teams face each other in Spain and the United States. During this camp, USWNT head coach Emma Hayes will get to see her squad face one of the top teams in the world as the road to the 2027 World Cup in Brazil continues. With players missing and depth concerns in defense, it's a good camp for Hayes to see what may need to change, and playing Spain twice allows time to tinker between games.Because of that, I took a look at some things to watch for during camp:Ashley Sanchez's role in a new positionOne doesn't tie the NWSL scoring record by accident, and no matter how you slice Ashley Sanchez's season with the N.C. Courage, it's quite impressive. But when peeling back how it's happening, that's when things get remarkable. For Sanchez's career, she has played as a striker or creative attacking midfielder, but in some of the best form of her career and earning the first national team call in two years, she's doing neither.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Head coach Mak Lind has come in and positioned Sanchez as a strict left winger. Playing as a right-footed forward on the left side, she's been able to cut inside, flip the ball to her right foot, and next thing you know, the keeper is picking the ball out of the back of their net. Looking at her finishes, it's easy to see why she has been overperforming her xG of 13.98. But even if that's stripped away, only Sophia Wilson has a higher xG on the season, and that's quite good company to be in. The front three of the USWNT is something which felt more settled than other positions on the pitch, but when someone is performing at Sanchez's level, they can't be left out of the national team, and that's a good problem to have when creating competition for the World Cup.Trinity Rodman is a creative forceLooking at one of the ways that Sanchez may get the ball, Trinity Rodman is the heartbeat of the attack because a defender never knows what she'll do. Already dynamic on the ball going forward, Rodman has a strong balance of scoring and creativity, and she could etch her name in NWSL history. In the NWSL regular season, there has never been a player to collect 10 goals and 10 assists in a season, and with 11 goals and eight assists, Rodman could do it with three games remaining in the Washington Spirit's season. She's not alone in chasing that as Cloe Lacasse and Pietra Tordin are also tracking to that number for the Utah Royals and Portland Thorns, respectively. There are a few reasons why so many players are on pace for something that has never been done before, as games have been added to the league and the quality of forwards entering has risen by the day, but a defense also doesn't know where Rodman will pop up to make them pay.

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Operating fluidly on the wing, she's just as likely to attack the box from the left as she is the right, and it helps make Hayes' USWNT unpredictable, which is important when facing Spain. If the USWNT aren't at their best, this will be a long international break, and Rodman is one of the keys to unlocking Spain's defense, as no matter where the other forwards move, she can move to set them up or generate her own shot.Does wing back Alyssa Thompson move back into the attack?Someone who generally operates as a forward, Alyssa Thompson has also undergone a position shift this season at Chelsea, moving slightly deeper to operate as a wing back. She has still been able to get in the box from left back, scoring a goal for Chelsea on 13 shots, but how this shift impacts her usage will be something to watch during this camp. On the one hand, becoming more well-rounded defensively could give the USWNT another wrinkle to unlock, but it could also lead to shifts among the forward line depending on how Hayes wants to set the squad up.Attacking-wise, with Sanchez here, there is a chance that Thompson isn't the top forward to bring into the game, but Hayes also doesn't set up in a back three, which is where things get a little wonky. At 21, she is among the members of the squad with the highest ceiling, but ceilings don't always lead to immediate minutes when there are matches to win.
Who is the secondary creator in midfield?Without Croix Bethune and Olivia Moultrie, midfield is thinner than expected, but Hayes could be able to plug Mal Swanson in wherever she needs as versatility grows among the attack. Swanson may have only played in 12 games this season for the Chicago Stars but she's been back in the lineup and performing well."She can play as the 10, she can play as the seven, the nine, the 11," Hayes said at her pre-match press conference. "When I think of a midfielder, I think of Lindsay [Heaps] Lilly [Yohannes]. I think she definitely looks more like herself and has made good progress since Brazil. I've seen some things in training this week that show she's on the right path, and 10 months postpartum, I don't think her road was easy so I expected things to take a little more time and support, but I think she's really finding her feet."Name-dropping Heaps and Yohannes shouldn't come as a surprise, as they'd be expected to take up the deeper roles in midfield, but who is ahead of them could be anyone's guess, as this is such a fluid team. That's a critical question to answer ahead of the World Cup too, as while some of the injured players could return by then, there is a need for depth in key positions.

body:
The USWNT will be without center back Naomi Girma and defensive midfielder Sam Coffey for this month's friendlies against Spain, who will ultimately test the hosts' depth in defense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For a team with the explicit goal of winning the Women's World Cup, there is no test more perfect than a pair of friendlies against the last team to take home the title. To do it a month before World Cup qualifiers and eight months before the tournament itself makes for perfect timing. The U.S. women's national team remain as well-equipped as any to handle the challenges Spain will pose over the next week, starting with Saturday's friendly in the nation's capital, but make no mistake – the circumstances are not exactly perfect.The reigning Olympic gold medalists are still the attack-minded force they have always been, but they will be understaffed for their doubleheader against Spain, and in a key area of the pitch. Center back Naomi Girma and defensive midfielder Sam Coffey were ruled out of the games with injuries, leaving the USWNT particularly understaffed in defense. Claire Hutton will likely fill Coffey's role and may have done so anyway, such is the quality of the 20-year-old. Head coach Emma Hayes has an eclectic group to work with at center back, though: Tierna Davidson, Girma's presumed partner at the World Cup next year; Tara Rudd, who joined the fold after the U.S. team won gold at the 2024 Olympics; Kennedy Wesley, who has seven caps; and Kate Del Fava, a first-timer with the senior national team after years of experience in the NWSL."Can't do anything about that," Hayes said candidly on Friday, though she does not exactly feel down on her luck.How to watch USWNT vs. Spain, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 10 | Time: 2:30 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: TBS | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: USWNT +260; Draw +250; Spain -110
"They're top players and I can put them in situations this week to create the exposures," she continued. "I think developing as a pairing is something that they're going to have to do, but I believe in them, and I watch their attention to detail. I think you got [Tierna], who, by nature, is a defender that can progress the ball up the pitch. Great covering defender, really good aerially. You got Kennedy, who steps to the play really well. I think they're actually a good complement to each other. I think they're very intelligent people, so they can solve really good tactical puzzles, and I've seen them do it all week, so I'm looking forward to seeing how they progress together."The 25-year-old Wesley is one of the late beneficiaries of Hayes' player pool expansion project following the Olympics but has been a focal point for the San Diego Wave, who remain in the hunt for the NWSL Shield thanks in large part to their league-leading defensive efforts. Her stock appears to on the rise and at a timely juncture in the USWNT's preparations for the World Cup, and Wesley seems to be soaking up every moment along the way."I think both Tierna, [Emily Fox], there are so many players that bring an ample amount of experience and it's been nothing so, so helpful to me, recognizing I can go to them with any question I have." Wesley said Thursday. "If I'm hesitant, they're always the first ones to kind of back me in my decisions, so it's been really awesome training with them the last few days and for the last few months, but I do think that their experience will help us propel in moments when we need it in the game. When we have long spells of defending, when the momentum might not be our way, I think those are players that I've relied on, the group can rely on in those really tough moments."
The group will perhaps be equally reliant on her on Saturday, Spain's impressive attack headlined by two-time Ballon d'Or-winning playmaker Alexia Putellas set to offer the USWNT's defense – understaffed or otherwise – their stiffest challenge yet. The U.S. team's defense has gone somewhat untested since the Olympics, with opponents averaging just seven shots per game and less than one expected goal along the way. The numbers are not all that different against teams ranked in FIFA's top 10, though Spain pose their own challenges."I think the first thing that comes to mind is that we're going to need to be really disciplined," Wesley said. "I think they're so dynamic in their movements, in their interchange when they have the ball, when they're in possession so it'll be really really important for us to be disciplined, not get pulled out of position so that we can kind of dispute their attack but I also think working form the back to front, it'll be really important we're really front-footed and pressing high on the field, not allowing them space and time because I think that's what they're the most successful so I think between the discipline and the front-footedness, I think those are really important."Chemistry questions are not reserved solely for the back line, even if they will be in focus as Spain attempt to impose their possession-oriented, attack-minded style. Hayes has spent the post-Olympic period expanding the player pool, tinkering with her lineups over the course of 30 games as she builds experience and depth in each area of the pitch. In both friendlies against Spain, though, she boasted that the lineups will be fairly similar and that the time for experimentation is essentially over. Though it is hard to envision a first-choice version of the USWNT without Girma in the lineup if she's available, Hayes might answer questions about who's leading the race for starting roles in attack at the World Cup.
Many of her mainstays are available, including the Triple Espresso – Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson and Mallory Swanson – though she is hardly limited in that department. Regulars including Alyssa Thompson, Emma Sears and Michelle Cooper are all amongst the bunch, and that group alone is a stark reminder that the U.S. team's historic attacking might is going nowhere."I think the cool part about the front line is that we all have chemistry in different ways," Wilson said. "I think we all can work together and kind of get the same product, and it doesn't really matter who's out there. I think we trust everyone to step up when their name is called. I think defensively, we really pride ourselves on being a high-pressing team and a team that wants to press and press with speed because I think we can create chances that way, and I think we have the players to do that, so just following that and knowing that's one of our strengths and I think it will be a strength against Spain."There are some newcomers in the group; their abilities to break into the core player pool still unclear. Trinity Byars and Pietra Tordin are amongst those who could earn their first cap, while Ashley Sanchez marks an impressive return to the national team around two years after she was last in the group. It is a well-earned return to the fold for Sanchez, who tagged along for the 2023 World Cup but has not been much of a fixture with the USWNT since. She leads the NWSL with 20 goals and is likely in the midst of an MVP-caliber season and, like Wesley, is also charting an upward trajectory at the right time.
"I think it's really cool and I'm obviously really proud of her," Rodman, her longtime teammate at the Washington Spirit before Sanchez's trade to the Courage in 2024, said. "I think through her career, she's been through a lot- ups and downs of coming into the national team, not starting, getting traded, and just so many things that I think that she's overcome, and even just playing in the midfield and now being the top goalscorer on the wing, I think, is really impressive, and I'm just really happy for her, and I do think this is her time, and I'm very excited to be able to share the field with her, and I think she deserves it. To be able to kind of play a lot of her career as a midfielder and to now thrive up top, I think, brings just another piece to the game and can also bring another type of forward to this lineup as well, which I think is really good for us."The fact that the USWNT enters their doubleheader against Spain with unanswered questions is intriguing in its own right; uncertainty rarely reassuring, no matter the circumstances. From the team's perch, though, it is all by design."Even [the World Cup] just being next year, I think we've already kind of got into that mindset, but obviously, we need to qualify," Wilson said. "But I think this team has been preparing for the World Cup since the day the Olympics ended. I think that's just the mindset, that everything we do in between these tournaments is just in preparation for the next."
